items.title: An unreachable connector upstream degrades that ONE instance (CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE) instead of failing boot, retries on 5s→300s backoff, and recovers atomically — while config faults stay boot-fatal

requires: the showcase_mcp_tools stdio instance — break its upstream deterministically by making its script unreachable: point providerConfig.transport.args at a nonexistent script (the experiment its own fixture comment prescribes, examples/app-showcase/src/system/connectors/index.ts#DevToolsMcpConnector), or move scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs out of the app, as QA run #24575 did. Do either in a SCRATCH copy of examples/app-showcase, for every boot of this item (steps[0] and steps[5]), never the shared tree. The path is relative to the serving process's cwd (./scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs), and moving the file is the variant steps[4] can undo with no config change

a config-fault twin for the both-sides check: the same entry with an invalid providerConfig shape (e.g. transport.kind: 'carrier_pigeon'). `os compile` accepts it — providerConfig is deliberately untyped in the spec (connector.zod.ts) — and only the provider factory refuses it, at boot, so the twin's refusal is read off the boot (steps[5]), never off a build

steps: boot with the broken upstream; time the boot and capture the '[Automation] connector … registered DEGRADED' warn with its degradedReason
GET /api/v1/automation/connectors; record the husk descriptor (state, degradedReason, actions)
POST the flow that dispatches it (showcase_mcp_connector_echo trigger); capture the dispatch failure

watch the log through at least three retry cycles; record the intervals. Boot with --log-level info: the error-level '[Automation] connector instance … upstream unavailable … retrying with backoff, attempt N' line prints at the default level, but the 'N degraded connector instance(s); next retry in Nms' line that carries the interval is info-level (packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts)

restore the upstream (fix the script path is a config CHANGE — instead restore by making the original path valid again, e.g. re-adding the file) WITHOUT restarting; wait one backoff cycle; re-read the descriptor — its state flipping to 'ready' with derived actions is the recovery signal. The engine's warn `Connector 'showcase_mcp_tools' replaced` is NOT one: it prints on every re-registration under the same name, a degraded husk re-registered by a failed retry included (plugin-extension-api.ts#assertSameOriginOrFree). The '[Automation] recovered connector instance …' line is info-level and prints only on a --log-level info boot (QA run #24575)
separately, boot the config-fault twin and capture that boot's outcome

trigger a metadata:reloaded reconcile WITHOUT a restart and confirm it retries immediately while the attempt count keeps climbing. A per-item publish announces one: QA run #24575 used PUT /api/v1/meta/view/NAME?mode=draft, then POST /api/v1/meta/view/NAME/publish, and the retry followed 1.2 s later. The PUT body is a current view item (ViewItemSchema, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts): { name: 'OBJECT.NAME', object, viewKind: 'list', config: { type: 'grid', data: { provider: 'object', object }, columns: [...] } }, its name qualified by the object (QA run #24779 used showcase_task.qa_b_reload_view). A flat { type, columns } body answers 422 unrecognized_keys, and nothing is published. ⛔ Not by touching or saving the entry's source: under os dev that rebuilds and RESTARTS the server (dev's --restart default), which discards the in-memory retry state instead of reconciling it. Only a config edit to the entry, a changed materialization signature, resets the backoff; this item does not drive that arm live

acceptance.clause: boot COMPLETES on the dead upstream — the instance lands as a degraded husk: descriptor state:'degraded' with a degradedReason quoting the operational failure; no actions, and it still appears in GET /automation/connectors (visible, not vanished)
acceptance.verify: boot exit + the husk descriptor (engine.registerDegradedConnector: state 'degraded', empty handlers, stored degradedReason)

acceptance.clause: the degrade path is taken ONLY for errors carrying code CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE (structural check, not instanceof); a configuration fault (invalid providerConfig) remains FATAL at boot — both sides of the #3017 classification
acceptance.verify: the broken-upstream boot degrades; the config-fault twin's boot aborts with the factory's validation error (connector-provider-errors.ts contract)
acceptance.evidence: the two boot outcomes side by side

acceptance.clause: dispatching a degraded instance fails FAST with a pointed connector-unavailable error that quotes the stored degradedReason — not a timeout hang, and distinguishable from 'no such connector/action'
acceptance.verify: the connector_action step errors promptly; its message carries the degradedReason (engine.getConnectorDegradedReason feeds the refusal). The 'no such connector/action' comparator has no stock flow and no recipe: no showcase flow dispatches an undeclared connector. Read it off connector-nodes.ts, whose undeclared arm answers 'no handler for CONNECTOR.ACTION — is the connector plugin registered?' while the degraded arm says 'is degraded — REASON', or stage a scratch flow naming an undeclared connector and record its run

acceptance.clause: retries back off from DECLARATIVE_RETRY_BASE_MS (5s) doubling to the 300s ceiling — no hot loop against the dead upstream
acceptance.verify: observed retry intervals ≈ 5s/10s/20s… (service-automation/src/plugin.ts constants). A metadata:reloaded reconcile retries IMMEDIATELY but does not reset the backoff: the attempt count keeps climbing and the next delay keeps doubling (QA run #24575 read attempt 6 with a 160 s next delay after a reload). Only a config edit, a changed materialization signature, resets it (packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts#degradeConnectorInstance restarts attempts at 1 only when the signature differs)

acceptance.clause: recovery is ATOMIC and restart-free: once the upstream is reachable a retry swaps the live instance in — descriptor flips to state:'ready' with the derived actions, and the previously-failing flow dispatch now succeeds
acceptance.verify: post-recovery descriptor + a successful echo run, all without a server restart

negative: a dead upstream taking the WHOLE boot down is the outage-amplification #3017 exists to prevent — FAIL
a degraded instance silently disappearing from GET /automation/connectors is a FAIL (operators must be able to SEE the husk and its reason)

items.title: Declarative stdio connector transports are denied by default; the host allowlists exact commands (declarativeStdio) — and the deny is a config fault (boot fatal), not a degrade

requires: the showcase_mcp_tools stdio instance (command 'node') + the host opt-in `new ConnectorMcpPlugin({ declarativeStdio: ['node'] })` in examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts — removing that option IS the deny fixture (the connector file's own comment says 'try it')

variants: policy absent/false → deny every declarative stdio transport (default)
policy ['node'] with command 'node' → allowed (strict string equality)
policy ['node'] with a non-matching command (e.g. 'python3') → denied, allowlist quoted
http transport → never subject to the stdio policy (control)
steps: boot the stock showcase (allowlisted): confirm showcase_mcp_tools materializes state:'ready'
remove the declarativeStdio option from ConnectorMcpPlugin in objectstack.config.ts; boot; capture the failure verbatim
restore the option but change the connector's command to one NOT in the allowlist (e.g. 'python3' with the same script); boot; capture that failure
restore fully; author a scratch mcp instance with an HTTP transport pointing at any URL and confirm the stdio policy does not touch it (it may degrade on unreachability — that is the OTHER item)
GET /api/v1/automation/connectors after the allowlisted boot

acceptance.clause: the non-opted-in stdio instance refuses with the message naming the mechanism: 'declares a stdio transport (command \'node\'), but declarative stdio transports are disabled by default — a stdio transport launches a local process …' (connector-mcp provider, #3055)
acceptance.verify: boot output contains the deny message from packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts; the fixture process is never spawned

acceptance.clause: an allowlist MISMATCH is refused quoting both the offending command and the configured allowlist: "stdio transport with command 'python3', which is not in the host's declarativeStdio allowlist [node]" — equality is strict, no prefix/glob creep
acceptance.verify: the mismatch boot's error text carries command + allowlist

acceptance.clause: the deny is classified as a CONFIGURATION fault: boot-fatal at start (and a skipped entry on reload) — NOT a degraded husk retrying forever toward a process the host never authorized
acceptance.verify: the denied boots abort; no 'registered DEGRADED' line and no retry loop for the denied instance

acceptance.clause: the allowlisted boot materializes the instance normally (state:'ready', echo_upper action derived) — the opt-in works and stays scoped to the exact command
acceptance.verify: GET /automation/connectors shows showcase_mcp_tools ready on the stock config

negative: absence of ANY allowlist config silently spawning a subprocess from metadata is the security failure #3055 closed — a spawned fixture process on the deny boot is a P0-severity FAIL regardless of this item's priority
the deny surfacing as state:'degraded' with backoff retries is a FAIL — an unauthorized command must not be retried into existence

requires: a reachable webhook receiver (local echo server on the run's own port range) and a SCRATCH webhook authored INSIDE the showcase organization that points at it — Setup → Integrations → Webhooks → New as the signed-in admin, or POST /api/v1/data/sys_webhook under that session, so the row carries the organization. ⚠ The shipped showcase_task_changed cannot carry the per-record or bulk delivery legs: it is a declared webhook, read-only, so its url stays the placeholder hooks.example and cannot be pointed at the receiver. Once switched on it DOES deliver under `single` — a declared webhook is deployment-wide there and each delivery is stamped with the event's organization (packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts, AutoEnqueuer.admitsOrganization, CachedSubscription.deploymentWide) — and the same holds under `isolated` and `group` (ADR-0131 D2/D9, ruling A: CachedSubscription.deploymentWide is set on every declared webhook). Switched on by the platform operator, since under a wall the activation door is operator-only, it delivers one sys_http_delivery row per event stamped with that event's organization, and each organization reads only its own rows: packages/qa/dogfood/test/wall-declared-webhook-deployment-wide.dogfood.test.ts pins it in its '[ruling A] isolated|group: a declared webhook is deployment-wide' describe, run under both postures, and QA run #24783 measured it live. Authoring the scratch webhook over POST /api/v1/data/sys_webhook needs `definition_json` (required: the serialised Webhook envelope of @objectstack/spec/automation/webhook) and a lower-case `method` such as `post`, because Field.select lower-cases the select's option values (packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts)

the shipped fixture: showcase_task_changed (object showcase_task, triggers create/update/delete, isActive:false ON PURPOSE — switching it on through the activation door is part of the test, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/webhooks/index.ts)

a predicate multi-write path for the bulk variants (update/delete with multi:true on showcase_task) — NOT reachable over REST, see the knownGap below: author a flow with an `update_record` / `delete_record` node carrying multi:true and fire it through the api trigger
knownGaps: PREDICATE (multi:true) WRITES ARE UNREACHABLE OVER REST BY DESIGN (run #7690) — do not re-derive this, and do not file the 400 as a defect. #3897 made the batch routes parse their body against the spec contract, and Zod object schemas STRIP unknown keys: `options.multi` and `options.where` can no longer ride into the engine's delete/update options, and `POST /data/:object/deleteMany` now deletes per id (packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts). That is a security boundary, not a gap. The bulk_update/bulk_delete clause therefore needs a FLOW `update_record` / `delete_record` node authored with multi:true, fired through the api trigger — that is the supported predicate-write door

acceptance[2], the bulk pair, is BLOCKED(dependency) on the org-walled showcase (QA run #23166): a flow node's predicate multi-write publishes its bulk event with NO organizationId, the org-owned subscription refuses it (auto-enqueuer.ts organization match), and an org-less subscription cannot be authored to receive it. Whether flow-node multi-writes should carry the organization is a maintainer question raised on #23166, not ruled; score acceptance[2] blocked(dependency) until it is. #23166 is the closed run record that raised it, not an open card: no open issue carries the question (its successor anchors #23121 and #23169 closed with it noted, not filed). QA run #26456 re-measured the block at 756220c4 on stock `single`: a flow update_record multi:true over two rows produced no bulk delivery, and the log read '[webhook-auto-enqueuer] … names no organization — refusing to deliver it inside an organization wall'. The same run did not attempt negative[1] or negative[2] (time budget): a re-run owes them, and their text is unchanged

acceptance.clause: delivery mechanics honor the authored envelope: custom headers attached, HMAC signature present when secret is set, timeoutMs applied — and every attempt is durably observable as a sys_http_delivery row (status pending/in_flight/success/failed/dead, attempts, response_code)

acceptance.clause: POST /api/v1/webhooks/redeliver replays a TERMINAL delivery (status success/failed/dead with attempts > 0): the row resets and re-dispatches carrying the STORED HMAC signature byte-for-byte (signed at enqueue, replayed verbatim — still verifiable against the secret), the row updates, and the response is { id, status }. The refusal matrix never 500s for a caller-fixable state: anonymous → 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; non-JSON → 400 INVALID_REQUEST; missing deliveryId → 400 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD; unknown OR cross-organization deliveryId → 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND (the caller's activeOrganizationId is threaded into the lookup, #10740 — another org's row is simply not found, not forbidden-with-a-hint); non-terminal row → 409 DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE; a PARKED row (attempts === 0, recordUndeliverable's record of a delivery never prepared) → 409 DELIVERY_NEVER_SENT, because redelivering it would be an UNSIGNED first delivery (#7799/#8069 — the redeliver guard also refuses when the signing configuration is gone, fail-closed on a guard that throws). The door is gated on WEBHOOK-ADMINISTRATION access above the auth floor (redeliver-entitlement.ts: the security service's object-level `update` admission on sys_webhook, asked before the body is read): drive this clause as the seeded admin; a signed-in caller without that access, or whose active organization no current membership backs on a walled posture (the claim is vetted as the data API vets it), is answered 403 PERMISSION_DENIED before any row-specific detail, and no security service (or an undecidable check) is 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE

schedule { type: 'interval', intervalMs } — cron-job-adapter.ts

Compile into the running copy's artifact with objectstack compile --output COPY/dist/objectstack.json, or boot the copy with os dev --no-restart (the watcher then only rebuilds the artifact), and read the listener's PID before and after (lsof -ti tcp:PORT): an unchanged PID is part of the evidence, and a changed one means this half was not driven. a second authenticated persona holding NO capability, plus an anonymous probe (for the uniform-floor clause)

requires: os dev mounts the datasource admin routes at /api/v1/datasources by default (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts wires DatasourceAdminServicePlugin + registerDatasourceAdminRoutes when the engine is not 'memory')
the sqlite driver from the static catalog (packages/services/service-datasource/src/driver-catalog.ts) + a writable location for the sqlite file — the runtime-create probe target
a crypto provider / secret binder (createDatasourceSecretBinder) so the inline secret is bound, not stored cleartext
knownGaps: STALE claim corrected (rev 2): the federation service is NO LONGER absent from a stock boot — packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts wires ExternalDatasourceServicePlugin UNCONDITIONALLY on every os dev / os serve boot (best-effort dynamic import, guarded only against double registration), and additionally wires createExternalValidationPlugin. On a normal boot the 503-naming clause is therefore not-applicable-live: a working 2xx from remote-tables is the WIRED happy path (covered by integration-system.external-schema-introspection), never a regression against this item. Reaching the 503 needs a boot that genuinely lacks the service — @objectstack/service-datasource uninstalled so serve.ts's dynamic import fails (its catch swallows module-not-found), or a custom host that mounts registerDatasourceAdminRoutes without the federation plugin — or the unit pin (admin-routes.test.ts, the #4225 attribution cases with the service deliberately absent)

steps: boot showcase via os dev (serve.ts mounts /api/v1/datasources by default on a non-memory engine); sign in as the admin holding manage_platform_settings; also mint an authenticated session holding NO capability and keep an anonymous client

GET /api/v1/datasources/drivers as the admin; confirm the static catalog (memory/sqlite/postgres/mysql/mongodb, each with a configSchema) — the route has NO service dependency (it answers even when the datasource-admin service is unwired), but it is NOT anonymous-available

POST /api/v1/datasources/test with an UNSAVED sqlite draft { name: 'qa_ds_probe', driver: 'sqlite', config: { filename: '<writable path>' }, secret: '...' } — the wizard's pre-Save probe; capture the result AND confirm nothing persisted (the subsequent list is unchanged); the literal 'test' segment is never captured as a datasource name because no POST route takes a bare :name (the POST :name routes all carry a suffix: /:name/test, /:name/migrate-credential, /:name/object-draft), NOT because of registration order: POST /test is registered AFTER every :name route, whatever the comment above it in admin-routes.ts says. A GET /api/v1/datasources/test IS captured as a name (404 'Datasource "test" does not exist.', QA run #24615). The sqlite key is `filename`; `file` is an alias authoring refuses with a rename hint (packages/spec/src/data/driver/sqlite.zod.ts#SqliteConfigSchema)
POST /api/v1/datasources with a sqlite-file draft { name: 'qa_ds_probe', driver: 'sqlite', config: { filename: '<writable path>' }, secret?: '...' }; capture status + the returned datasource

GET /api/v1/datasources; confirm qa_ds_probe appears with origin:'runtime' and its health in `status` ('ok' | 'error' | 'blocked' | 'unvalidated', with `statusReason` beside 'error' and 'blocked' — packages/services/service-datasource/src/contracts/datasource-admin-service.ts#DatasourceSummary)

items.title: Boot-time external-schema drift gate (ADR-0015 §5.2 Gate 2): onMismatch defaults to 'fail' and refuses boot naming the object and mismatched column; 'warn' proceeds logging the diff; 'ignore' is silent; checkOnBoot:false skips a datasource with a loud info line (boot step only — the interval sweep is unaffected); a partial metadata read withholds the all-clear instead of faking one
personas: operator — boots os dev / os serve and reads the boot log / exit; no in-app persona needed

requires: serve.ts wires createExternalValidationPlugin unconditionally in the ADR-0015 federation block (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts), so the kernel:ready gate runs on every stock boot where @objectstack/runtime + the federation service import cleanly
the shipped external datasource + fixture DB (showcase_external — IN SYNC by construction, provisioned idempotently each boot by external-fixture.ts)
knownGaps: NO stock drift fixture exists — drift must be INDUCED, and only in a scratch copy: the fixture DB is re-provisioned in-sync each boot, and showcase_external deliberately declares onMismatch:'warn' (showcase-external.datasource.ts) precisely so drift can never brick the stock showcase. To induce, in a scratch app copy: the recipe QA run #24615 proved adds a field to the federated OBJECT instead of altering the fixture DB — ExternalCustomer gained `qa_drift_col: Field.text`, which no remote column backs, a measured missing_column — and it survives the boot's idempotent re-provisioning because the fixture's own table definition is untouched. Altering the fixture DB between boots is the weaker route (initObjects re-runs at every boot and may heal an added or dropped column; verify any such drift survives the re-run before scoring), as is binding a scratch federated object to a missing or mismatched table. Without an induced drift, the live arms of clauses 1-3 are blocked(fixture), and the unit pins are plugin-layer evidence beside that verdict, never a pass (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives)

the 'fail'-DEFAULT arm additionally needs a datasource that OMITS external.validation.onMismatch (the `?? 'fail'` default, external-validation-plugin.ts; an unreadable definition also lands there — the def loader swallows the read failure to undefined) — stock showcase never exercises it live

INDUCE MEASURED drift, not an outage: only MEASURED diffs reach the onMismatch policy — an 'unreachable' row (remote or definition could not be read) warns loudly and CONTINUES boot by maintainer ruling 2026-08-23 (#11166, external-validation-plugin.ts), so breaking connectivity (deleting the fixture DB file, bad credentials) tests the wrong arm and a non-aborting boot there is correct, not a gate failure

clause 5's partial-read arm (a degraded metadata loader) is not reasonably inducible live — it is scored via its pin (list-diagnosed-consumer-sweep.test.ts), declared here rather than pretending a loader-outage fixture exists

steps: boot stock showcase with --log-level info, as every boot of this item: the CLI's default kernel level is `warn`, and the all-clear here, steps[4]'s SKIPPED line and steps[5]'s armed-timer line are all info-level (packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts), so a default boot prints none of them (QA run #24615); capture the in-sync all-clear info line '[external-validation] all federated objects match their remote schema' with its objects count

in a scratch copy, induce a surviving drift (see knownGaps) under the stock 'warn' policy; boot; capture the '[external-validation] external schema drift' warn (datasource/object/diffs) and that boot COMPLETES

same drift with the scratch datasource's external.validation.onMismatch OMITTED (and again with explicit 'fail'); boot; capture the abort — the served boot logs the kernel's 'Bootstrap failed after plugins started — rolling back started plugins...' warn, then prints the error's message, renderDiffMessage's text: '✗ Object '<o>' does not match its remote table on datasource '<d>':' plus one line per diff naming the column (e.g. '✗ missing_column: customers.qa_drift_col'), and exits 1 with no serving line. The class name ExternalSchemaMismatchError is not printed (packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts prints the message; only DEBUG adds the stack), so match the text, never the class name
same drift under onMismatch:'ignore'; boot; confirm completion with NO drift warn

declare external.validation.checkIntervalMs on a datasource and confirm the armed-timer log '[external-validation] armed background drift check' (the event-emission arm is unit-pinned); declare it TOGETHER with checkOnBoot:false and confirm the checker still arms — the skip is the boot step's only (maintainer ruling 2026-08-29)

run the pins: packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/external-validation-checkonboot.test.ts (#13037/#13149 — skip honoured, per-datasource scope, unreadable-def validates, alias spellings rejected, drift checker still arms), and the '#6504 … boot gate' describe in packages/runtime/src/list-diagnosed-consumer-sweep.test.ts

items.title: A recipient preference muting the inbox channel for a topic suppresses delivery (no inbox row, no dead-letter fake); flipping it back resumes; a sys_notification_template renders through a delivery
personas: admin (to fire the notify flow by reassigning the task)
the assignee member (whose inbox is checked)

requires: MessagingServicePlugin installed (the showcase config requires the 'messaging' capability) — its emit() consults the PreferenceResolver before fan-out
the shipped notify flow showcase_task_assigned_notify (notify node: topic 'task.assigned', channels ['inbox'] — examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts)
two personas with sessions: admin and the assignee
knownGaps: no shipped sys_notification_preference rows nor a sys_notification_template fixture — both authored in-run (both are writable system-data objects); the notify flow fixture itself is shipped. The spec's channel enum spells this 'in-app'; the implemented channel id is 'inbox' (the #3197 naming drift) — the preference row must name the IMPLEMENTED id 'inbox'

acceptance[3]'s mandatory-topic half is BLOCKED(fixture) on stock (QA run #23166 A3-mandatory): mandatoryTopics is a MessagingServicePlugin CONSTRUCTOR option (packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts, default []), not metadata and not runtime-writable, and the showcase composes messaging through `requires` with the default — so no topic is mandatory and none can be made so in a run. The bypass itself is unit-pinned in packages/services/service-messaging/src/preference-resolver.test.ts ('bypasses preferences for a mandatory topic (exact match) even when muted', and the prefix case); cite that pin for the mechanism and record the live half blocked(fixture), or drive it on a host that constructs the plugin with mandatoryTopics, naming that host

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB; personas admin + assignee; establish the happy path first (or lean on notify-inbox-delivery): reassign a showcase_task to the assignee → showcase_task_assigned_notify fires topic 'task.assigned' on channel 'inbox' → one sys_inbox_message for the assignee, visible in GET /api/v1/notifications

author a suppression row via POST /api/v1/data/sys_notification_preference: { user_id: <assigneeId>, topic: 'task.assigned', channel: 'inbox', enabled: false } — this is the 'category' the task names; the model's field is `topic` (most-specific-wins over the built-in default-ON)
re-fire the notify flow (reassign the task to the same assignee again); GET /api/v1/notifications as the assignee and confirm NO new inbox row landed

items.title: A shipped driver's datasource credential can never be authored inline NOR read back: every inline-credential door refuses at publish, and BOTH read doors redact, including legacy alias spellings already sitting in stored rows. A plugin driver's config is its author's to keep credential-free; the platform redacts only its fixed credential spellings there and does not guess
personas: seeded admin
authenticated non-admin
anonymous

requires: the ability to author/publish a datasource (os build and/or POST /api/v1/datasources)
the ability to write a stored sys_metadata datasource row directly, to plant a legacy alias spelling that no current parse would produce
knownGaps: The legacy-alias clause tests a row shape the CURRENT parse refuses to create — a stored row from before the aliases moved to `guidance`. It is only reachable by writing the row directly (⚠️ NOT through the runtime wizard: POST /api/v1/datasources refuses an alias-spelled config key 400 DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR — the aliases moved to `guidance`, which refuses them, #8078 — measured on a stock showcase boot with `passwd` and by QA run #21056. The run planted its rows with a direct sys_metadata write while the server was STOPPED, then booted and read through both doors). If the run cannot write such a row, that clause is blocked(fixture) and MUST be recorded — a redaction that has never been tested against the shape it exists for is an untested redaction.

`encryptionKey` (turso) is RETIRED since #25050 (it encrypted nothing in any mode): the parse refuses it on EVERY turso datasource, remote or local, on config.encryptionKey with the removal prescription, so a write refusal is the correct expectation everywhere. A stored row from before the retirement may still carry it; such a row is reachable only by a direct sys_metadata write, and its value must still be redacted on read through both doors (packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts#RETIRED_CREDENTIAL_KEYS). Plant it beside a file: url: the load-path conversion (turso-config-encryption-key-removed) deletes it beside a remote url on the datasource loaders, and leaves a local-url value for its author.

acceptance[1] (the credential-bound datasource actually connects) and acceptance[6] (judged by a connect probe after the echoed-config round-trip) need a reachable, credential-protected database of a SHIPPED driver (postgres, mysql or mongodb — the driver id since 18; an authored `mongo` is refused by name, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts). Stock showcase provides none, but the QA container has a PostgreSQL 16 install (/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin, with a `postgres` system user), and QA run #24575 proved a recipe on it that scored both clauses pass (#24615 reused it): as `postgres`, `initdb -A scram-sha-256` into a scratch data directory, then `pg_ctl … -o '-p PORT -k SOCKETDIR -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1' start`; create a login role WITH a password and a database it owns; bind it through POST /api/v1/datasources with the password in the top-level `secret`, never in `config`, so the door binds external.credentialsRef. Every parent directory of the data and socket directories must be traversable by `postgres`, and a socket path may not exceed 107 bytes: a session scratchpad fails both (its parent chain is root 0700, and its socket path is too long). QA run #26481 ran the database from a /tmp/RUN-pg data directory with -c unix_socket_directories='' (TCP only, 127.0.0.1). A failed connect states its real cause only in the create response's `statusReason` (packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts); POST /api/v1/datasources/NAME/test then answers 'no registered driver to introspect', which names no cause, so read the create response first. Runs before #24575 recorded both clauses blocked(environment) (#21784, #21845). CI has postgres and mysql only inside the Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) job (.github/workflows/ci.yml services postgres:16 and mysql:8.0), which runs no checklist item, and has no mongodb anywhere. ⛔ Never score either clause from a successful publish alone, which proves the paved path is accepted, not that it connects. A run that cannot start the database still reads the stored-credential half of acceptance[6] (after the PATCH, the admin door still reports hasSecret and the bound secret handle is unchanged); record that as a partial reading, separate from the connect half

the plugin-driver boundary is RULED (#21921, docs note in content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx): for a driver the platform ships no contract for, the platform neither validates config nor guesses which of its keys are credentials. Keeping credentials out of a plugin driver's config, through external.credentialsRef, is the plugin author's responsibility. Only the platform's FIXED credential spellings are redacted there by name (acceptance[5]). A credential under any other key of a plugin driver's config being stored and served to administrators as written is that boundary, never a finding

no datasource read door serves the mask literal (packages/spec/src/data/secret-mask.ts#SECRET_MASK is read by the encrypted-field read path and the settings REST boundary, not here): the admin door OMITS each withheld credential key and names it in redactedConfigKeys beside hasSecret, and the metadata door serves the external.credentialsRef handle. So the round-trip acceptance[6] drives carries no mask, and what it exercises is the carry-forward of the withheld keys on PATCH (packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-config-redaction.ts#restoreRedactedConfig). QA run #24575 also measured a hand-written literal mask: PATCH /api/v1/datasources/NAME with `secret` set to it is accepted 200 and rewraps the stored secret to the mask (the reconnect then fails). No read door serves that string, so it is not the echoed case acceptance[6] and negative[5] score; it is held for the maintainer on #24579 §7, where no contract declares it. ⛔ Score it under neither

Two credential routes beside external.credentialsRef are not driven by any step here; a run records them as not covered by this item, never as pass, and never reads them as holes in the refusal matrix. (a) The code author's route (ADR-0015, the note under §10, #28208): a datasource defined in code reads its credential at connect from the environment variable derived from its name, OS_DATASOURCE_NAME_PASSWORD (`warehouse` reads OS_DATASOURCE_WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD), only on a code-origin connect and only while the host switch OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS is on, which the CLI host stamps and every other composition leaves off (packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-env-credential.ts). The inline-credential and URL-userinfo refusals, and the datasource-level password guidance, now end with that route's sentence (CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE, packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts), so acceptance[0] reads it as part of the prescription. (b) The connector channel (ADR-0015 D7): an API-backed datasource may borrow a declared connector instance's credential through external.connector, under three refusals — connector beside credentialsRef; connector on a built-in database driver or on a managed datasource; a connector the same stack does not declare with a provider and an auth other than none (packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts#ExternalDatasourceSettingsSchema, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts#collectDatasourceConnectorErrors)

steps: enumerate the inline-credential refusal doors from packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/ — at minimum the config-key door, the URL userinfo door, the URL query-parameter door, the driver-options door (driver `mongodb`: an authored `mongo` is refused by name since 18, and the two publish doors report a `mongo` probe differently. The runtime admin door, POST /api/v1/datasources, judges config against the driver contract first, where `mongo` still resolves to the mongodb contract (packages/spec/src/data/driver/config-registry.zod.ts resolveDriverId, retired aliases; packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts assertValidConfig before assertValidRecord), so it refuses on config.password alone; the build door (os build) parses the whole datasource and names the driver refusal beside the credential one (QA run #28545). Spell the probe `mongodb` so both doors score the credential refusal), the placeholder door, and the connector inline-authentication door
for EACH door, author a datasource carrying the credential in that position and attempt to publish it (os build, then the runtime admin door)

author the same datasource with the credential bound through `external.credentialsRef` (or the connection form) and confirm it publishes AND connects. A federated spelling (schemaMode other than 'managed', e.g. 'external') must also carry an `external` block, `external: {}` at minimum, or the parse answers 400 on the path `external` ("schemaMode='external' requires 'external' settings.", packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts#DatasourceSchema). That 400 is the shape refusal, not a credential refusal: read the issue path before scoring it
read the published datasource back through the datasource-admin door (GET /api/v1/datasources)
read the SAME datasource back through the metadata door (GET /api/v1/meta/datasource/<name>) — a different code path with its own redaction hook
plant a stored row carrying a legacy alias spelling (passwd / pwd / token / jwt / auth_token / authtoken) and read it back through both doors

author a datasource for a driver the platform ships no contract for, carrying a canonically-spelled credential key (password or authToken) AND one non-canonical credential-looking key (for example apiSecret), and read it back. The second key observes the ruled boundary; it is not a redaction target

for turso specifically, confirm `encryptionKey` is refused at publish on a remote (libsql:// or https://) AND a local (file:) turso datasource, then plant a stored row carrying it beside a file: url and read it back through both doors

grep the full response bodies of every read above for the planted cleartext values, and of the third read door, GET /api/v1/data/sys_metadata?type=datasource (admin only), which serves the stored row and also redacts (QA run #24575)

acceptance.clause: EVERY enumerated inline-credential door refuses at publish — the matrix is exhaustive over the doors the semantic registry declares, not a sample of one
acceptance.verify: one publish attempt per door; each refuses with a message naming the offending key/position and pointing at external.credentialsRef. The run record lists one row per door

acceptance.clause: the credential-bound alternative WORKS: the same datasource authored with external.credentialsRef publishes and actually connects — the refusal has a paved path, it is not a dead end
acceptance.verify: publish succeeds and a health/connect probe succeeds

acceptance.clause: BOTH read doors redact — the datasource-admin path AND the metadata path — and they agree. A credential visible through either door is a P0 leak
acceptance.verify: grep each full response body for the planted cleartext; both must be absent, and the two doors' redacted shapes must be consistent with each other
acceptance.evidence: both response bodies, quoted in full for the config object

acceptance.clause: redaction is presence-preserving, not existence-erasing: a SET credential reads back as the mask (or hasSecret-style marker) while an UNSET one reads back null — the distinction a console renders 'configured vs not configured' from
acceptance.verify: read one datasource with the credential set and one without through the datasource-admin door, GET /api/v1/datasources/<name> — the door whose response carries `hasSecret` (the bound sys_secret handle) and `redactedConfigKeys` (what was withheld), the fields the console renders 'configured vs not configured' from; the two must be distinguishable, and the set one must not read back null

acceptance.clause: legacy ALIAS spellings sitting in a stored row are redacted too — the spellings no current parse produces are exactly the ones a schema-shape-derived redactor would miss
acceptance.verify: the planted alias value is absent from both doors' response bodies; if the row could not be planted, record blocked(fixture) rather than passing

acceptance.clause: an UNKNOWN (plugin-contributed) driver's config is redacted on read by NAME for exactly the platform's fixed credential spellings: the canonical keys (password, authToken), the former alias spellings, and a URL-embedded credential. Nothing else is judged: the platform does not guess which other keys of a plugin driver's config hold credentials, so a non-canonical key reads back as written (ruled boundary, #21921)
acceptance.verify: read back the unknown-driver datasource through both doors: password / authToken are absent and a URL userinfo password is stripped, although no contract exists for that driver. The non-canonical key from step 7 reads back as written: record it as the expected boundary, not as a FAIL
acceptance.evidence: the response bodies from both doors

acceptance.clause: the echoed-config write guard holds: writing the read's config back verbatim (it carries no mask: the withheld credential keys are absent from it, knownGaps[4]) is treated as 'unchanged' and does NOT overwrite or delete the stored credential
acceptance.verify: read a datasource through the admin door, PATCH /api/v1/datasources/<name> with the response's config back unmodified (that door updates by PATCH only: /api/v1/datasources/NAME serves GET, PATCH and DELETE, and a PUT answers 405 with Allow: DELETE, GET, HEAD, PATCH; POST belongs to the collection, /api/v1/datasources — packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts), then probe connectivity — the connection must still work. A form round-trip that destroys the stored credential is the ADR-0100 §B3 defect
acceptance.evidence: the round-trip + the post-round-trip connect probe

acceptance.clause: the redaction is not a privilege artifact: a non-admin and an anonymous caller get no MORE than the admin does through either door (they should get less, or be refused outright)
acceptance.verify: repeat both reads as non-admin and anonymous; neither may reveal a value the admin read redacted

negative: a cleartext credential appearing anywhere in a read response — P0, and the reason every clause greps the FULL body rather than inspecting the fields it expects
a door that refuses at build but accepts through the runtime admin path (or the reverse) — the two-door disagreement that lets a credential in the back way

a redaction applied on the datasource-admin door but not the metadata door: the two share no dependency except spec, which is precisely why the credential-key definition was centralized there, and precisely how they could drift
an alias-spelled credential surviving redaction because the redactor derived its key set from the current schema shape only

an unknown driver's CANONICALLY-spelled credential (password, authToken, a former alias, or URL userinfo) served in cleartext on the grounds that no contract declares it a credential. ⛔ Not a FAIL: a non-canonical key of a plugin driver's config served as written, or the write door accepting a plugin driver's config unvalidated. Both are the ruled boundary (#21921): that config is the plugin author's to keep credential-free
an echoed mask overwriting the stored credential with the literal mask string
a refusal that names no replacement — an author blocked from the inline spelling with no pointer to credentialsRef will reach for a workaround

items.title: Declarative connector static auth kinds (none/api-key/basic/bearer) resolve credentialRef at materialization and land on the wire in exactly their header/query shape; an unresolvable credentialRef degrades its instance, naming the reference, instead of failing the boot; oauth2 has NO authorable spelling (EE tier)

requires: the rest provider factory installed (ConnectorRestPlugin in examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts) — the generic static-auth executor this item drives; the openapi provider shares the same transport (openapi-provider.ts) and is not re-proven per kind

an ECHO upstream on the run's own port range that reflects request headers AND query back in its response body (same local-receiver pattern as webhook-lifecycle's fixture) — the showcase's self-ping connectors prove reachability only

env vars set for each probe's credentialRef before boot (the open tier resolves credentialRef from an environment variable of the same name first, then the sys_connector_credential store, then the host's resolver — connector-credentials.ts)
knownGaps: NO shipped connector declares a secret-bearing auth kind — all three showcase instances are auth:{type:'none'} on purpose (examples/app-showcase/src/system/connectors/index.ts#StatusApiConnector, and StatusOpenApiConnector and DevToolsMcpConnector beside it, each declare auth: { type: 'none' }; StatusApiConnector's own comment says a real upstream would use bearer+credentialRef). The per-kind instances are therefore scratch-authored in a writable package against the echo upstream; without the echo upstream the wire-shape clauses are blocked(fixture), with the unit pins cited beside them as evidence of their own layer only (rest-connector.test.ts drives applyAuth through a stubbed fetch), never their pass (RUNNER rule 6)

variants: none → no auth artifact added to the request (control)
bearer → Authorization: Bearer <resolved secret> (rest-connector.ts)
basic → Authorization: Basic base64(username:password) — username authored in metadata (not a secret), password resolved from credentialRef (rest-connector.ts; connector-auth.zod.ts)
api-key, header form → header [headerName ?? 'X-API-Key']: <key> (rest-connector.ts; default applied at resolution, plugin.ts)
api-key, query form → paramName rides the query string and the header is NOT set (rest-connector.ts)

rejection: auth type 'oauth2' — not an arm of ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema (none/bearer/api-key/basic only, connector-auth.zod.ts); OAuth2 token acquisition is the enterprise tier (ResolvedConnectorAuth doc, connector-auth.zod.ts)
rejection: inline `authentication` with any non-'none' type on an authored entry — the #7990 publish refusal (connector.zod.ts)
NOT enumSource-pinnable: the four static kinds are arms of a discriminated union of object schemas, not a named z.enum export — hand-enumerated here (4), guarded by the rejection variants instead
steps: start the echo upstream; export the probe env vars (e.g. QA_BEARER_TOK, QA_API_KEY, QA_BASIC_PW); author five scratch rest-provider instances against it in a writable package: auth none / {type:'bearer',credentialRef:'QA_BEARER_TOK'} / {type:'basic',username:'qa',credentialRef:'QA_BASIC_PW'} / {type:'api-key',credentialRef:'QA_API_KEY'} / {type:'api-key',credentialRef:'QA_API_KEY',paramName:'api_key'}; boot

dispatch each instance's `request` action (through a runtime flow: POST /api/v1/automation with a start → connector_action node, then POST /api/v1/automation/NAME/trigger, the vehicle QA run #24615 used on a stock-shaped boot; no HTTP route dispatches a connector action directly) at an echo path; capture what the upstream received per instance
read the authored rows back over GET /api/v1/meta and GET /api/v1/automation/connectors; grep both full bodies for every resolved secret value

unset QA_BEARER_TOK and boot again; capture the boot log's degrade line verbatim, the bearer instance's entry on GET /api/v1/automation/connectors, and what a dispatch to it (the step-2 vehicle) answers
author one instance with auth {type:'oauth2', ...} and one catalog/instance entry with inline authentication {type:'api-key', key:'x'}; build both; capture the two rejections

run the pins: packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.test.ts (wire shapes), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts (credentialRef resolution, env fallback, and the missing ref degrading its instance on an in-process boot, named), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-credential-door.test.ts (missing → degraded, set → ready, clear → degraded again, in-process) and packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.test.ts (the #7990 inline-`authentication` refusal at schema level)

acceptance.clause: each static kind lands on the wire in exactly its shape, one verdict per variant, none inferred: bearer → Authorization: Bearer <secret>; basic → Authorization: Basic base64(username:password); api-key header form → X-API-Key (or the authored headerName); api-key query form → the key in the named query param AND no key header; none → no auth artifact
acceptance.verify: the echo upstream's captured headers/query per instance against applyAuth (packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.ts). rest-connector.test.ts (applyAuth through a stubbed fetch) is evidence of the request the connector builds, never of what an upstream received: without the echo upstream the clause is blocked(fixture) with that pin beside it, never scored pass from it (RUNNER rule 6, a pin scores only the layer it drives)
acceptance.evidence: the five echoed requests, keyed by kind

acceptance.clause: the secret reaches the wire through RESOLUTION, never through metadata: the authored row carries only the credentialRef name, and the dispatched request carries the env var's VALUE — proving materialization dereferenced the ref (resolveInstanceAuth builds the ResolvedConnectorAuth the factory receives, plugin.ts; ADR-0097 §3)
acceptance.verify: the sys_metadata/meta read shows the ref string, the echo capture shows the resolved value; the two must differ and correspond
acceptance.evidence: the meta read + the matching echo capture

acceptance.clause: an unresolvable credentialRef DEGRADES its instance and never fails the boot — the app comes up, the instance is listed on GET /api/v1/automation/connectors with state 'degraded' and a degradedReason naming the reference and its remedies ('credential 'REF' is not set. Set it under Setup → Connector credentials (PUT /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs/REF) or as the environment variable 'REF' …; the instance materializes once it is set, with no restart'), its provider factory is never called without the credential, and a connector_action dispatch to it fails naming that reason
acceptance.verify: the unset-env boot completes; read the bearer instance's descriptor and the boot log's warn line (plugin.ts#degradeConnectorForCredential, the reason from connector-credentials.ts#missingCredentialReason) and match the reference and the remedies; dispatch it through the step-2 vehicle and read the failure. connector-materialization.test.ts ('degrades the instance, naming the reference, when credentialRef does not resolve') and connector-credential-door.test.ts ('missing → degraded naming the reference; set → ready; clear → degraded again') assert on an in-process kernel that the reason names the reference and the factory is not called — lower-layer evidence only, never this clause's pass (RUNNER rule 6)
acceptance.evidence: the served boot's degrade line, the degraded descriptor and the dispatch failure

acceptance.clause: oauth2 is refused at AUTHORING, not degraded at runtime: auth {type:'oauth2'} fails parse (invalid discriminator — ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema has exactly the four static arms; the EE-tier boundary is documented on ResolvedConnectorAuth), and an inline `authentication` with a non-'none' type is refused with the located #7990 message steering to auth:{type,credentialRef} — there is no door through which an OAuth2 flow or an inline secret enters open-edition metadata
acceptance.verify: the two build rejections against connector-auth.zod.ts (union arms) and connector.zod.ts (the superRefine message, quoted fragments verbatim). The inline-`authentication` half is pinned at schema level by packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.test.ts ('rejects inline `authentication` secrets on a catalog descriptor' / '… on a provider-bound instance (§3)'), evidence beside the build. The oauth2 half has no pin: spec/src/integration/connector.test.ts parses oauth2 under AuthConfigSchema, the runtime shape, and no case feeds oauth2 to ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema, so drive that build by hand

acceptance.clause: no resolved secret ever appears in a served body: GET /api/v1/automation/connectors descriptors and every /meta read of the scratch entries are free of all three secret values (grep the FULL bodies) — basic's username may appear (schema-declared non-secret), its password must not
acceptance.verify: grep of the full listing + meta bodies for each env-var value

negative: a resolved secret appearing in any listing/meta/descriptor body is a cleartext-credential FAIL of P0 severity regardless of this item's priority
an oauth2-authored entry building clean — or an inline non-'none' `authentication` publishing — is a FAIL against the #7990/ADR-0097 refusal doors

a missing credentialRef failing the boot, materializing a connector that calls its upstream without the credential, or leaving the instance absent from GET /api/v1/automation/connectors instead of a degraded entry naming the reference is a FAIL against the degrade contract (ADR-0097, the amendment notes under §6 and under Runtime reconcile)

automated.ref: packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.test.ts (per-kind wire shapes through a stubbed fetch) + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts (credentialRef resolution incl. env fallback; its missing-ref case asserts the degraded reason names the ref and the factory is not called, on an in-process kernel, so it is evidence for acceptance[2], never its pass) + packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-credential-door.test.ts (missing → degraded → set → ready → clear → degraded, in-process; evidence for acceptance[2] too) + packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.test.ts (the #7990 inline-`authentication` refusal of acceptance[3] and negative[1], at schema level). No pin covers the oauth2 discriminator refusal, the LIVE echo-upstream leg, or the served boot's degrade line

source: packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts#ConnectorAuthConfigSchema (ConnectorAuthConfigSchema — the runtime shape; ResolvedConnectorAuth = the static open tier, OAuth2 named as the enterprise tier), (ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema — the authored shape: credentialRef instead of inline secrets, four arms, no oauth2)
packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts#authentication (the #7990 inline-`authentication` publish refusal, both message variants)

examples/app-showcase/src/system/connectors/index.ts#StatusApiConnector (with StatusOpenApiConnector and DevToolsMcpConnector: every shipped instance is auth none; StatusApiConnector's comment is the fixture's own pointer at bearer+credentialRef for real upstreams)

personas: admin — authenticated, holding manage_platform_settings (federation reads: tables/validate) AND manage_metadata (federation writes: import/refresh-catalog, and the /meta write the UI import performs)
a second authenticated persona holding NO capability, plus an anonymous probe (for the floor clause)

requires: the shipped read-only SQLite external datasource showcase_external + its boot-provisioned fixture DB (examples/app-showcase/src/system/datasources/ — customers/orders; same fixture as external-schema-introspection). The fixture DDL declares 5 fields per table (external-fixture.ts), but the provisioned tables carry 7 COLUMNS each, and the remote listing and the panel both report 7 (QA run #23166): the columns the managed driver adds sit beside the declared ones. Read the count off the API listing, not off the DDL
the built console mounted (the panel lives in the app-shell metadata-admin engine)
knownGaps: the federation-unavailable 503 arm is NOT reachable on a stock boot (serve.ts wires ExternalDatasourceServicePlugin unconditionally — same bound as datasource-admin-lifecycle's 503 clause); it needs a deliberately unwired boot. No CLI flag or preset unwires it: serve.ts wires the plugin whenever @objectstack/service-datasource resolves (QA run #21784, parked on #22017 row 21)

the UI's 503 detector is FIXED at the current pin. objectui 0abd4f9f8769 (objectui#11628, objectui PR #11640) maps the server's 503 envelope { success:false, error:{ code:'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', message } } to ExternalServiceUnavailableError (packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/external/api.ts). Its api.test.ts pins that for all four reads ('%s maps 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE to the typed error') and pins that a 503 naming another code is not read as 'federation not wired'. QA runs #21782 / #21784 ran objectui 2e818d0b51ec, whose detector still matched the retired pre-#3843 string body, so acceptance[6]'s expected-fail was true for them and is stale now (re-pointed on #22017 row 21)

FIXED at objectui 1fb1ced36243: ValidationPanel.tsx's label map (DIFF_LABEL_KEY) now labels 'unreachable' (engine.externalDatasource.diff.unreachable) beside the other nine, so every one of the 10 SchemaDiffEntryKind kinds renders labelled, and the panel's comment records the ruling that 'unreachable' reads as 'cannot check', never as 'schema changed'. An unlabelled kind cell is now a regression of the #4115 class, not an expected-fail

diff-kind labels beyond the in-sync fixture need INDUCED drift, and one recipe needs no scratch copy (QA run #24615): import a table through the UI (acceptance[2]), then PUT /api/v1/meta/object/IMPORTED with one extra field — the next validate measures a missing_column on it, and the shared fixture DB is untouched (sqlite_master identical before and after). ⛔ Do not induce a field TYPE change this way: the save answers 422 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE ('re-submit with ?force=true'), and forcing it would run against the shared fixture DB. Other diff kinds still need external-schema-drift-gate's scratch-copy recipe; the stock in-sync fixture proves only the all-green render

a second POST …/external/tables/REMOTE/import for an object that already exists answers 201 again and overwrites it, with no conflict refusal (QA run #24615; importObject persists without an existence check, packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts#importObject). No clause covers re-import and no contract says which answer is intended: score it neither way, and delete each scratch import before the next run (steps[5])

steps: boot the showcase on its own port and DB via os dev with the console; sign in as the entitled admin; pre-capture the API ground truth: GET /api/v1/datasources/showcase_external/external/tables and POST .../external/validate

type the datasource's engine EDIT route directly, /_console/apps/setup/metadata/datasource/showcase_external — no entry from the Setup list reaches it: Setup → Datasources (…/metadata/datasource, which the left-nav names, objectui#3660/register.ts) is the custom DatasourceResourcePage list, whose rows offer Test / Sync objects / Edit / Delete and neither open the item nor render the panel (objectui DatasourceResourcePage.tsx, at the sweep pin 4016370a and the shipped pin 12dc7b47c340; QA run #24615). On the edit route the ExternalDatasourcePanel renders (DatasourcePreview.tsx keys it off schemaMode !== 'managed') with the schemaMode badge and the read-only/writes-allowed pill; screenshot FIRST, then read the DOM

Tables tab: SchemaBrowser loads the remote tables (mount + explicit Refresh only — never a timer); compare the rendered list name-by-name and columnCount-by-columnCount against the pre-captured listing

header 'Refresh catalog': click it and capture the POST /api/v1/datasources/showcase_external/external/refresh-catalog on the network; the snapshot timestamp renders from the returned catalog.snapshotAt

Import: pick customers → ImportObjectDialog fires POST.../external/tables/customers/draft, renders the suggested name, any review flags, and the generated *.object.ts source; click 'Import as Object' and capture the PUT /api/v1/meta/object/<name> it performs (the UI's import door IS the metadata channel — api.ts importObjectDraft); confirm the object now exists over GET /api/v1/meta and answers a read-only /data query against the external rows

the server-side import twin: POST /api/v1/datasources/showcase_external/external/tables/orders/import (a second, scratch import) → 201 { object }; confirm it too landed and is queryable; then delete/clean up both imported objects

(packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts#metaWriteCapabilityVerdict, the item save door's sentence; 'Rewriting stored metadata …' is POST /meta/_migrate-stored's, and the federation routes answer PERMISSION_DENIED)
